title: A Garden for the Hollow Anew
premise: Yara Nystrom, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics they shape, keeps quiet ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things in a city built atop a drowned country. When a dying courier presses a map of doors into their hands—doors out of a nation that was officially erased from history forty years ago—the Guild's masters, the Hollow Court, want it back, and they will hollow out anyone who has touched it. Hunted by the Court's bone-puppets and guided by the stubborn ghost of the courier, Yara gathers a found family of the unregistered: a disgraced dragon-keeper, a child who remembers the old country, and a rival carver who once betrayed them. As the last dragon-fire gutters in the mountains, Yara learns the doors open only for those who belong somewhere—and that belonging must be built, not found. In the end, Yara chooses to stay behind and hold the final door open, letting their found family pass into the restored old country while they carve the Court's power apart from within; the epilogue reveals the door can be reopened, and the family returns for them.
about_author: Freya Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of people with no one left to claim them, an experience that haunts every page of her fiction. She writes fantasy about the paperwork of grief, the geography of belonging, and the small rebellions of quiet people.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Unclaimed Things
chapters.summary: Yara Nystrom's POV. In the Guild's counting house, Yara carves a dead woman's fingerbone into a key and hears her last words: a name, a debt, a door. The chapter establishes the bone-carving gift, the Guild's quiet menace, and Yara's strategy of invisibility. Beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Weighing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A bleeding courier collapses into the Guild's weighing room during the quarterly audit, pressing a folded map into Yara's hands and whispering 'the doors are real' before dying. Yara hides the map in a hollowed bone rather than report it. Beat: the first crack in a carefully maintained invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Hollow Court Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with a brief interlude from Guildmaster Vess. Yara glimpses the Court's inner vault—shelves of carved bones, each one a silenced person—and realizes the courier's death will be noticed. Vess begins asking pointed questions. Beat: dread; the reader learns the stakes of being noticed.

chapters.title: The Ghost Who Won't Settle
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The courier's ghost, Oren, manifests through a carved knucklebone and refuses to fade, demanding his map be delivered to 'the keeper of the last fire.' Yara, who has always treated the dead as cargo, argues with a voice that treats them as a person. Beat: reluctant connection.

chapters.title: The Dragon-Keeper of Ashfall
chapters.summary: Oren's map leads Yara to the mountain town of Ashfall and to Sef, a disgraced dragon-keeper tending the guttering last dragon, Vhalor, in secret. Sef recognizes the map's seal and nearly turns Yara in. Beat: wary alliance born of shared fear.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef introduces Yara to Pip, an unregistered child born after the old country's erasure who nonetheless remembers its streets in dreams. Pip's dreams match Oren's map exactly. Beat: wonder; the possibility that the erased can be recovered.

chapters.title: Bone Puppets in the Market
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Hollow Court's bone-puppets arrive in Ashfall, wearing the faces of the dead Yara has carved. One speaks with the courier's stolen voice. Yara and Sef flee with Pip through the ash-fields. Beat: horror; the past weaponized against them.

chapters.title: The Rival Carver
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In a border refuge, they find Ilsabet, Yara's former mentor and the carver whose testimony once got Yara's sister registered—and lost. Ilsabet offers help but Yara cannot forgive her. Beat: bitterness; the cost of old betrayals.

chapters.title: Doors Are for Those Who Belong
chapters.summary: Ilsabet's POV. Ilsabet explains the map's rule: the doors out of the erased country open only for people who belong to it, and belonging is a thing that can be given, sworn, or carved. The group realizes Pip may be the key. Beat: the theme crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Court's Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vess catches up to them—not with puppets, but with an offer: return the map and Yara's sister, still held in the Court's registry, will be freed. Yara, tempted, nearly accepts. Beat: temptation; power corrupting through kindness.

chapters.title: What Oren Carried
chapters.summary: Oren's ghost POV. Oren finally remembers why he took the map: he wasn't a courier but a Court clerk who discovered the erasure was a land-grab, not a mercy, and stole the doors to give the country back. Beat: revelation; the map is restitution, not escape.

chapters.title: The Fire Gutters
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Vhalor the dragon is dying; her fire is the only thing keeping the old country's borders from collapsing entirely into the Court's possession. Sef confesses they have been prolonging her death for years out of love. Beat: grief; the cost of holding on.

chapters.title: Sworn in Bone
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara performs the forbidden rite of sworn belonging: carving a piece of their own bone into a token for Pip, making the child theirs—and making Pip a child of the old country by adoption of the living. Beat: found family made literal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Ilsabet's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilsabet's POV. Ilsabet reveals she registered Yara's sister to save Yara from the Court's purge, trading one sibling for another, and has spent fifteen years carving counterfeits to smuggle the erased out. Yara's forgiveness begins. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Counting House
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To reach the first door they must pass through the Court's vault, where every silenced voice is shelved. Yara plans to wake them all. Sef objects; Pip insists the dead deserve to be heard. Beat: moral resolve before the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Night of a Thousand Voices
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, ensemble. Yara shatters the vault's silence-charms; the dead rise as voices, not puppets, overwhelming the Court's enforcers. Vess, exposed, reveals the Court's masters were the architects of the erasure. Beat: triumphant chaos; the turning point.

chapters.title: Vhalor's Last Flame
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The group reaches the mountain as Vhalor dies. With her final fire she burns away the false border the Court drew, and her death-heat forges the first door into being. Oren's ghost passes through, finally at rest. Beat: sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: The Door That Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The door stands open, but it will close forever when the last ember of Vhalor's fire cools. The Court, desperate, moves to seal it from the other side with an army of puppets. Yara realizes someone must stay to hold the hinge. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Who Stays
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Each member offers to stay; Yara, as the only one who can hear and command the awakened dead, is the only one who can hold the door. Pip refuses to leave; Yara lies to the child with a carver's steady hands. Beat: heartbreak disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sef, Ilsabet, and Pip pass through into the restored old country as the puppet army breaks against the wall of risen voices Yara conducts. Yara holds the door as the ember cools, watching their family walk into a country that exists again. Beat: the climax's emotional peak—loss as gift.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court, Unmade
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Alone with the dead, Yara turns the Court's own ledgers against it, carving the masters' crimes into bone that cannot be silenced. The Court collapses; the erased are named, counted, and mourned. Yara, hollowed but unbroken, begins carving a new door. Beat: justice and quiet rebirth.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Hollow Anew
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, years later. In the old country, Pip tends a garden grown over Vhalor's ashes. One morning the old door, long cold, warms—Yara's carving has finally opened it from the far side. The family walks through to find Yara waiting, and the dead at rest behind them. Beat: belonging, earned and returned.
